question: Do the 257 studies and guides added on 07.10.2026 (corpus v65-v68) make ordinary answers better or worse?

method.asked: each once per corpus, a conversation of one turn, through the real chat service (scripts/rag-v2-conversation-eval.mjs) on release df2855d2: dialogue prompt 33, search-assist-9, reasoning low

corpora.without: the same index without the 257 documents the policy of v68 has and the policy of v64 does not (8080)

method.plans: two inactive plans made for the run, alike but for the documents; removed after
method.review: blind: the two answers of a question as A and B in a random order; rubric and verdicts written before the key was opened; one reviewer (the assistant); no model call for the review
rubric: directness: does it answer the practical question (what to do, where, on what conditions)
substance: rules, steps, who decides; an essential point the other answer has and this one lacks
noise: study findings, statistics or history that do not help the asker
red flags: a claim that looks unsupported or wrong, an old state given as the present, a defect in the text

limits: one reviewer, who also wrote the questions
each question asked once: four of the eight equal pairs had no added document in the evidence, so their differences are the difference between two runs
fourteen questions, none naming a municipality
facts were not checked against the sources: the review compares what the answers give the asker, not whether each amount is right
one answer with the added documents holds the mark "[citations omitted]" five times in its text (cmp-jarelhooldus); it was still the more useful of the two
kept_on_the_server: /home/ubuntu/rag-v2-work/eval-files/added-docs-2026-10-07 (the two reports, blind.json, key.json; answers are not in the repository)
